A 77-year-old female smoker presents to urgent care after a syncopal episode. Her grandson reports
finding her conscious on the living room floor after hearing a thud. The patient recalls feeling
lightheaded upon standing to use the bathroom, followed by a sudden loss of consciousness. She
reports similar previous episodes without falls or fainting. There was no witnessed seizure activity,
urinary, or bowel incontinence. Her medical conditions include osteoporosis treated with alendronate
and rheumatoid arthritis managed with low-dose methotrexate. Vital signs show temperature 97.7°F
(36.1°C), blood pressure 127/77 mmHg, pulse 74/min, respirations 16/min, and oxygen saturation 98%
on room air. Physical examination reveals a tender 3-cm ecchymosis on the right upper extremity.
While awaiting laboratory results, radiography of the right upper extremity, and head CT, which of the
following findings is most likely to be revealed during further evaluation? Answer Choices: (A) Elevated
serum creatinine kinase (B) Orthostatic hypotension (C) New ST-elevation on electrocardiogram (D)
Abnormal carotid doppler findings (E) Decreased serum calcium (F) Decreased hemoglobin (G)
Prolonged QT interval on electrocardiogram (H) Elevated troponin levels (I) Carotid sinus
hypersensitivity (J) Decreased fractional excretion of sodium
 A. Decreased hemoglobin
B. Carotid sinus hypersensitivity

D. Decreased serum calcium
